Mika: Several origins: Finnish and Japanese short forms, Hebrew 'who is like God' as a short form of Michael, and a Native American 'raccoon'. Often a pet form of Michael.
Tina: Short form of names ending in -tina, such as Christina or Martina, from Latin 'Christian' or 'of Mars'.
Madeline: English form of Madeleine, from Mary Magdalene, 'of Magdala', a town on the Sea of Galilee.
Lenthe: Dutch, from lente 'spring' (the season), a modern Flemish girls' name.
Léane: French, probably a variant of Léa or Liane, or from Leanne. Origin uncertain; Léa is from Hebrew 'weary' or Latin leo.
Sky: English word for the heavens, used as a modern given name.
Seb: Short form of Sebastiaan or Sebastian, from Greek sebastos 'venerable, revered'.
Elza: Variant of Elsa, a short form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Used in Slavic and Baltic regions.
Ilya: Russian form of Elijah, from Hebrew Eliyahu, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Iliano: Modern name, probably from Italian or Spanish Iliano, perhaps related to Elias or Iliad. Origin uncertain.
Salih: Arabic, meaning 'righteous, virtuous'. Salih was a prophet in the Quran.
Thyméo: Modern French name, probably built from Timéo or Thymeo with Greek thymos 'spirit' or Timothy. Origin uncertain.
Carolina: Latin and Italian feminine of Carolus, Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Zofia: Polish form of Sophia, from Greek sophia, 'wisdom'.
Zümra: Turkish, from Arabic zumra, meaning 'group, band' (as in a company of people).
Noan: Modern name, probably a Breton or French variant of Noé or Noah. Origin uncertain.
Linne: Dutch and Scandinavian, probably from Linnea or Lina. Also an English place name. Origin uncertain.
Vladimir: Slavic, from vlad 'rule' and mir 'peace' or 'great', so 'ruler of peace' or 'famous ruler'.
Eileen: Irish and English, from Eibhlín, a form of Evelyn or Helen, perhaps 'light' or 'pleasant'.
Houdayfa: Arabic Hudhayfa, perhaps 'little ostrich' or from hadhafa. Borne by a companion of the Prophet; meaning uncertain.
Dayana: Variant of Diana, Latin goddess; from Latin dius, 'divine, heavenly'.
Lyah: Variant of Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'. Origin uncertain.
Nala: Sanskrit and Swahili, 'gift'; also the Lion King lioness. Used in various cultures.
Tomás: Spanish, Portuguese and Irish form of Thomas, from Aramaic 'twin'.
Aysha: Variant of Aisha, Arabic, 'alive, living, well'. Borne by the Prophet Muhammad's wife.
Ahsen: Turkish, from Arabic ahsan, meaning 'best, most beautiful'.
Cézar: Portuguese and French variant of Caesar, Latin, probably 'hairy' or 'cut'. Roman family title.
Ade: Yoruba, meaning 'crown', a short form of many Yoruba names; also a short form of Adele or Adrian. Origin varies.
Bibi: Pet form of various names, or Persian and Urdu 'lady'. Also a short form of Babette. Origin uncertain.
Afnan: Arabic, meaning 'branches' (plural of fann), referring to boughs of trees.
Ghali: Arabic, meaning 'dear, precious' or 'expensive'. Used in North Africa.
Almila: Turkish, probably from Turkic al 'red' and mila 'apple'-like meaning, or an invented name. Origin uncertain.
Ouways: Arabic Uways, a diminutive of aws 'wolf' or 'gift'. Uways al-Qarani was a revered early Muslim ascetic.
Éléna: French form of Helena, from Greek 'torch' or 'bright one'.
Alfons: Germanic, from adal 'noble' and funs 'ready', via Spanish Alfonso. A Dutch form.
Elyon: Hebrew, meaning 'highest', used as a name for God, El Elyon.
Isaia: Italian form of Isaiah, Hebrew 'Yahweh is salvation'.
Justine: French feminine of Justin, from Latin iustus, 'just, fair'.
Quinten: Dutch form of Quentin, from Latin Quintinus, from quintus 'fifth'.
Sander: Dutch, Norwegian and Estonian short form of Alexander, Greek 'defender of men'.
Mike: English short form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Margo: Short form of Margaret or Margot, from Greek margarites, 'pearl'.
Timothy: English form of Greek Timotheos, 'honouring God'. A companion of Saint Paul.
Soufiane: North African form of Sufyan, Arabic, meaning 'swift' or 'one who sails'. Sufyan al-Thawri was a famous scholar.
Maité: Basque and French, from Maite, 'beloved'; also a form of Maria Teresa.
Anass: Arabic Anas, meaning 'friendliness, affection'. Anas ibn Malik was a companion of the Prophet.
Annabel: English, probably a variant of Amabel, Latin 'lovable', or a compound of Anna and Belle.
Danté: Italian, a short form of Durante, Latin durans 'enduring'. Made famous by the poet Dante Alighieri.
Lora: Variant of Laura, from Latin laurus, 'laurel'. Also a Slavic name.
Jasmijn: Dutch spelling of Jasmine, from Persian yasmin, the jasmine flower.
Iluna: Basque, meaning 'darkness' or 'dusk'; sometimes used as a modern, possibly invented, girl's name. Origin uncertain.
Bruce: Scottish, from the Norman surname de Brus, from Brix in France. A royal Scottish name.
Dana: Several origins: Hebrew 'judge', Persian 'wise, knowledgeable', Irish 'Danu'. Used for both sexes.
Helin: Turkish, probably from Helen or Turkic, meaning 'the beloved one'; also a Kurdish name. Origin uncertain.
Noémi: French and Hungarian form of Naomi, Hebrew 'pleasantness'.
Matthéo: French variant of Matteo or Matthieu, from Hebrew Matityahu, 'gift of God'.
Ilyano: Modern name, probably blending Ilyan or Ilyas (Elijah) with the ending -o. Origin uncertain.
Rodrigo: Spanish and Portuguese, from Germanic Hrodric, 'famous ruler'.
Dominik: Central European form of Dominic, from Latin dominicus, 'of the Lord'.
Ceylin: Turkish, from ceylan 'gazelle', as in Ceylan.
Mikael: Scandinavian and Breton form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Raven: From the English bird name, from Old English hraefn; also a modern given name.
Vasco: Portuguese and Galician, probably from Basque 'Basque' or a short form of Velasco. Origin uncertain.
Abigaëlle: French feminine variant of Abigaël, from Hebrew 'my father is joy'.
Camiel: Dutch form of Camille or Camillus, a Roman name of uncertain origin, perhaps 'attendant of rites'.
Laszlo: Hungarian form of Ladislaus, from Slavic Vladislav, 'ruler of glory'.
Luke: English form of Greek Loukas, 'man from Lucania'. Also a short form of Lucius, 'light'.
Lavinia: Latin, the wife of Aeneas in Roman myth. Origin uncertain, possibly 'of Lavinium'.
Noélia: Spanish and Portuguese form of Noel or Noelle, from Latin natalis 'birth', i.e. Christmas.
Astor: From a French surname, meaning 'hawk' (Old French, from Latin astur). Also used as a Spanish name.
Milano: Italian for the city of Milan; used as a given name. Also a form of Milan, Slavic mil 'dear'.
Elis: Welsh and Scandinavian, a variant of Elias or Elijah, or a short form of Elisabeth. Used for both sexes.
Oone: Probably a Dutch variant of Oona, Irish Úna, 'lamb' or 'one'. Origin uncertain.
Alara: Turkish, a name used for girls, possibly from Alara river or 'bright'. Origin uncertain.
Madina: Arabic, 'city', referring to Medina, the holy city of Islam.
Chams: Arabic, shams 'sun', as used in North African French spellings of Chams.
Leeroy: English or French, from Old French le roi, 'the king'. Used in English-speaking countries.
Lyas: Variant of Ilyas or Elias, the Arabic form of Elijah, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Adaline: Variant of Adeline, from Germanic adal 'noble'.
Hektor: Greek, from Hektor, 'holding fast' or 'steadfast'. The Trojan prince in the Iliad.
Estera: Romanian, Polish and Spanish form of Esther, Persian 'star' or Hebrew 'I will hide'.
Moise: French form of Moses, probably from Egyptian mose 'child, son'.
Jounayd: Arabic Junayd, a diminutive meaning 'little soldier' or 'warrior'. Borne by the Sufi Junayd of Baghdad.
Éline: French, a variant of Aline or Eline, perhaps from Adeline 'noble'. Also Dutch pet form of Helena. Origin uncertain.
Liyo: Modern name, possibly a variant of Leo or Lio. Origin uncertain.
Freyja: Old Norse, 'lady'. The Norse goddess of love and fertility.
Riv: Possibly a short form of names like Rivka or Rivers, or Hebrew Riv 'quarrel'. Origin uncertain.
Aqsa: Arabic, meaning 'farthest', as in Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.
Layel: Probably a variant of Layal, Arabic 'nights'. Also used as Arabic Layla's variant. Origin uncertain.
Lieze: Flemish short form of Elisabeth or Liesbeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Timo: Finnish, German and Dutch short form of Timotheus, Greek 'honouring God'.
Dimitri: Russian and French form of Greek Demetrios, 'follower of Demeter'.
Karel: Czech and Dutch form of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Liza: Short form of Elizabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Also a Russian form.
Bavo: Flemish, from Saint Bavo of Ghent. Probably Germanic in origin; the meaning is uncertain.
Damon: Greek, from damazo 'to tame, subdue'. A legendary friend of Pythias.
Aleandro: Italian, a form of Alejandro or Leandro, 'lion-man' or 'defender of men'. Origin uncertain.
Kira: Russian, from Greek kyrios 'lord'; also Persian 'sun' and a Japanese name. Used in many cultures.
Bernard: Germanic, from bern 'bear' and hard 'brave, hardy'.
Rami: Arabic, meaning 'archer'. Also a Hebrew short form of Ramiel.
Erva: Turkish, possibly from Arabic arwa, 'more refreshing' or from erva. Origin uncertain.
Angèle: French form of Angela, from Greek angelos, 'messenger, angel'.
Manoah: Hebrew, meaning 'rest, resting place'. Father of Samson in the Bible.
Eléanor: French and Spanish variant of Eleanor, perhaps from Provençal Aliénor, of uncertain origin, possibly 'other Aenor'.
Karina: Scandinavian and Slavic form of Karin, from Katherine, Greek 'pure'. Also Latin carina 'keel'.
Youssouf: West and North African form of Yusuf, the Arabic Joseph, 'God will add'.
Rozanne: Variant of Roseanne, a blend of Rose and Anne. English and Dutch.
Erina: Japanese 'pear' or 'child of grace' depending on characters; also a variant of Irene. Origin uncertain here.
Olive: English, from Latin oliva, the olive tree, a symbol of peace.
Emna: North African variant of Amina, Arabic 'trustworthy, faithful'.
Luuk: Dutch form of Luke, from Greek Loukas, 'man from Lucania'.
Filippa: Italian and Swedish feminine of Philip, from Greek 'friend of horses'.
Soren: Danish form of Latin Severus, 'stern, serious'. A Scandinavian name.
Kiyan: Persian, meaning 'king', or Kurdish 'sovereign'. Also used in Turkey.
Chani: Hebrew short form of Chana (Hannah), 'grace, favour'. Also a character in Dune.
Tjeu: Dutch, a Limburg short form of Mathieu or Mathijs, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Timotei: Romanian form of Timothy, from Greek Timotheos, 'honouring God'.
Nela: Slavic short form of Petronela or Manuela, or of Cornelia. Origin uncertain.
Amana: Arabic, meaning 'trust, safekeeping'; also a Hebrew place name. Used for girls.
Ilinca: Romanian, a diminutive of Ileana (Helen), from Greek 'torch, bright'.
Rayyan: Arabic, meaning 'watered, lush', and the name of a gate of paradise.
Davi: Portuguese form of David, from Hebrew 'beloved'.
Mousa: Arabic form of Moses, probably from Egyptian mose 'child'.
Éden: French form of Eden, Hebrew 'delight' or Sumerian 'plain'. The biblical garden.
Manoë: Modern French name, perhaps a blend of Manoah or Noë. Origin uncertain.
Attila: Gothic, from atta 'father' with a diminutive suffix, so 'little father'. Hungarian use.
Léone: French feminine of Léon, from Latin leo, 'lion'.
Ize: Probably a short form of Isabel or Izegrim, or a Dutch coined name. Origin uncertain.
Fill: Probably a short form of Filip or Phillip, from Greek 'friend of horses'. Origin uncertain.
Asaël: French form of Asahel, Hebrew 'God has made'. A biblical figure.
Arham: Arabic, meaning 'most merciful'; also a Jain Sanskrit name for 'worthy'.
Gigi: Pet form of names such as Gisèle, Virginia or Luigi. Italian and French.
Lennert: Dutch form of Leonard, from Germanic leon 'lion' and hard 'brave'.
Fiona: Scottish, from Gaelic fionn 'fair, white'. Coined by James Macpherson in the 18th century.
Shana: Hebrew 'beautiful'; also an English variant of Shannon and a form of Sean. Origin varies.
Rayane: Arabic Rayyan, meaning 'watered, lush', and a gate of paradise. Also Rayan.
Myriam: French form of Miriam, Hebrew; possibly 'beloved' or 'wished-for child'.
Marvin: English from Old English 'sea friend', or a Welsh Merfyn. Also a variant of Mervyn.
Sonia: Russian pet form of Sofia, from Greek 'wisdom'.
Jinte: Dutch, probably a Frisian pet form of Jantine or Jacinta. Origin uncertain.
Ibe: Basque and Frisian, probably from Ibe, a Germanic short name. Also West African; origin uncertain.
Nicholas: English form of Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'.
Xavi: Catalan short form of Xavier, from Basque Etxeberri 'new house'.
Ziggy: Pet form of Siegfried or Zygmunt, Germanic 'victory peace'. Also associated with David Bowie's Ziggy Stardust.
Célian: French, from Latin Caelianus, 'heavenly', a form of Caelius.
Noura: Arabic, meaning 'light, radiant'. A feminine of Nur.
Pietro: Italian form of Peter, from Greek petros, 'rock'.
Philippine: French feminine of Philippe, from Greek Philippos, 'friend of horses'.
Pénélope: French form of Penelope, Greek, possibly 'weaver' (pene 'thread'). The wife of Odysseus.
Aurélia: Latin feminine of Aurelius, from aureus, 'golden'.
Mahdi: Arabic, meaning 'guided one', the rightly guided. A messianic title in Islam.
Alperen: Turkish, from alp 'hero, brave' and eren 'saint, holy man'.
Aksel: Scandinavian form of Absalon, Hebrew 'father of peace'. Also used in Turkey as an unrelated name.
Aubin: French form of Albinus, from Latin albus, 'white'. A Breton saint.
Nélia: Portuguese and French variant of Nelia, probably a short form of Cornélia. Origin uncertain.
Lorik: Probably Albanian, a variant of Lorik or Lorenc, of Latin 'laurel'. Origin uncertain.
Eben: Hebrew, meaning 'stone'. A biblical name element, as in Ebenezer, 'stone of help'.
Sohaib: Arabic Suhayb, a diminutive of ash-shuhba 'greyish-red'. Borne by a companion of the Prophet.
Alena: Slavic, a form of Helena, Greek 'torch, bright'.
Raymond: French and English, from Germanic ragin 'counsel' and mund 'protector'.
Solal: Hebrew-based, possibly from Sol 'sun' or Sephardic Solal. Also a Jewish North African surname. Origin uncertain.
Tilly: English pet form of Matilda, Germanic 'mighty in battle'.
Uriel: Hebrew, 'God is my light'. An archangel.
Roger: Germanic, from hrod 'fame' and ger 'spear'. Norman import to English.
Antonella: Italian diminutive of Antonia, from the Roman family name Antonius, of uncertain meaning.
Meysa: Arabic Maysa, meaning 'to walk proudly' or 'swaying gracefully'.
Sulayman: Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew shalom 'peace'.
Maylo: Modern name, possibly a variant of Mailo or Milo. Origin uncertain.
Eliakim: Hebrew, meaning 'God will establish'. A biblical name.
Kays: Arabic Qays, possibly 'firmness' or a Quraysh tribe. Famous from the poet Qays of the Layla story.
Odilon: French, from Germanic uodil 'inheritance, wealth'. Saint Odilo of Cluny.
Alaya: Sanskrit, meaning 'abode, dwelling'; also a modern Arabic variant of Alia. Origin varies.
Emiliana: Latin feminine of Aemilianus, from the Roman family name Aemilius.
Tasneem: Arabic, 'a spring in paradise', also meaning 'raised high'.
Alin: Romanian male name, from Slavic or Latin alinus; also Turkish 'forehead'. Origin uncertain.
Lyaz: Probably a variant of Lyas or Ilyas, Arabic Elijah, 'my God is Yahweh'. Origin uncertain.
Ottilie: French, German and English from Germanic odal 'prosperity'. Saint Odilia.
Femke: Frisian and Dutch, a diminutive of Fem or Femme, from Old Frisian fenne 'girl, maiden'.
Kaat: Dutch short form of Katharina, from Greek katharos, 'pure'.
Audrey: English, from Old English Æthelthryth, 'noble strength'. Saint Etheldreda.
